instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Cut the peppers into 2 inch pieces, discarding the stems and seeds. Quarter the tomatoes and cut the onion into wedges. Leave the garlic cloves in their skins.
Spread the vegetables and garlic in a single layer on a large rimmed baking sheet, using two sheets if they are crowded. Toss with the oil, 3/4 tsp salt and the pepper.
Roast 45 minutes, turning everything halfway, until the edges are charred and the tomatoes have collapsed.

Squeeze the garlic out of its skins into a blender. Add the roasted vegetables with all the juices from the pan and the 2 cups broth. Blend until smooth, in two batches if needed, holding the lid down with a towel. Add a splash of water if you'd like it thinner.
Pour the soup into a pot and warm it over medium about 5 minutes, until it is steaming and just bubbling. Take it off the heat and stir in the vinegar and the last 1/4 tsp salt.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

Serve hot. For packed lunches, cool the soup, then keep it in the fridge up to 5 days or in the freezer up to 3 months. Reheat it until steaming, then pour it into a thermos that you've warmed with boiling water.
method_notes: About 60 minutes, almost all of it hands off in the oven, so it suits making on a weekend and packing for the week. Healthy Living James (4.96 from 45) is the lead: roast tomatoes, red peppers, onion and garlic in one tin, then blend with stock, no cream. It uses a stock pot, so this version uses real vegetable broth and a little more oil to help the edges brown. A teaspoon of red wine vinegar after the heat is off comes from Sinful Kitchen, which finishes its soup the same way. Veggie Society roasts the peppers under a broiler and simmers the soup with smoked paprika, and Marin Mama Cooks adds carrots and celery; none of that is in here.
